quickAnswerTitle: Indiana School Calendars Are Set Locally
quickAnswer: Indiana does not publish one statewide K–12 attendance calendar. A featured 2026–27 comparison includes M.S.D. of Wayne Township, Hamilton Southeastern Schools, Indianapolis Public Schools, and Fort Wayne Community Schools, whose opening dates run from July 29 through August 12. State law supplies the instructional baseline, but families need the calendar for the assigned district, school, or program.
about:
Indiana school calendars are published locally rather than as one statewide student schedule. State law establishes instructional-time requirements, while school corporations publish the first day, last day, breaks, staff days, eLearning dates, conferences, and make-up rules families actually use. Those local schedules can differ substantially even within the same metropolitan area.

A featured comparison uses reviewed 2026–27 calendar data for Fort Wayne Community Schools, Hamilton Southeastern Schools, Indianapolis Public Schools, and M.S.D. of Wayne Township. Wayne Township begins July 29 and uses two-week fall and spring recesses. HSE begins August 5 and states that virtual learning days will be used if school is canceled. IPS begins August 10 and counts three student asynchronous-learning days within its published 180 student days. FWCS begins August 12, with separate Transition Day and Pre-K details on the district calendar.

A districtwide calendar may not cover every school or program. IPS Innovation Network schools can publish separate calendars or operating decisions, Wayne Township lists program exceptions to its Monday late-start schedule, and FWCS separates selected-grade Transition Day and Pre-K opening dates from the main first student day. Families should confirm the calendar assigned to the student before making childcare or travel plans.
calendarRulesDescription: Indiana sets the instructional baseline; local school corporations publish the dates and calendar terms that apply to students.

calendarRules.label: No statewide student calendar
calendarRules.description: First days, breaks, staff dates, eLearning schedules, make-up rules, and last days come from local district and school calendars.

calendarRules.label: At least 180 instructional days
calendarRules.description: Indiana Code generally requires a school to conduct at least 180 instructional days during each school year. Statutory flexibility and approved waivers can apply in qualifying circumstances.

calendarRules.label: Minimum instructional-day length
calendarRules.description: The state minimum is five hours of instructional time for grades 1–6 and six hours for grades 7–12. Lunch and recess do not count as instructional time.

calendarRules.label: Nine-month school-year minimum
calendarRules.description: Indiana Code sets a minimum school-year length of nine months, while the actual attendance dates remain local.

calendarRules.label: eLearning is not automatically a vacation day
calendarRules.description: A district may label asynchronous or synchronous eLearning as instruction outside the normal in-person schedule. Read the event description before treating the date as a student day off.

faqs.q: Does Indiana have one statewide public school calendar?
faqs.a: No. Indiana sets instructional-time requirements, but local districts publish the dates students attend. First days, breaks, eLearning dates, staff days, make-up rules, and last days vary by district and sometimes by school or program.

faqs.q: When do Indiana schools start in 2026?
faqs.a: There is no single statewide start date. Among the reviewed 2026–27 calendars, M.S.D. of Wayne Township starts July 29, Hamilton Southeastern Schools starts August 5, Indianapolis Public Schools starts August 10, and Fort Wayne Community Schools starts August 12.

faqs.q: How many instructional days are required in Indiana?
faqs.a: Indiana Code generally requires at least 180 instructional days in a school year. IDOE also notes statutory flexibility for qualifying schools and an instructional-day waiver process.

faqs.q: Do Indiana districts have the same spring break?
faqs.a: No. In the reviewed 2026–27 calendars, IPS lists Spring Break for March 15–19, FWCS lists Spring Vacation for March 29–April 2, and Wayne Township lists Spring Recess for March 29–April 9.

faqs.q: Are asynchronous eLearning days days off in Indiana?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. IPS and Wayne Township use asynchronous eLearning labels for instructional days outside the normal in-person schedule. Check the district's event description before arranging childcare or travel.

faqs.q: Why can an Indiana school use a different calendar from its district?
faqs.a: A district calendar may be only the baseline. IPS Innovation Network schools can publish separate calendars or operating decisions, Wayne Township lists program exceptions to its Monday schedule, and FWCS separates some grade and Pre-K opening dates.

faqs.q: Can I add an Indiana school calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. Reviewed Indiana district pages provide ICS files for Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook. The import is a one-time snapshot and will not automatically reflect later district revisions.
